solution: The sequence \(9-8i,\ 8-6i,\ 7-4i,\ \ldots\) is an A.P. with first term \(a = 9-8i\) and common difference \(d = (8-6i)-(9-8i) = -1+2i\). So \(T_n = a+(n-1)d = (10-n) + i(2n-10)\). \(T_n\) is real when the imaginary part vanishes: \(2n-10 = 0 \Rightarrow n = 5\). The 5th term is real.
\(60(a+59d) = 40(a+39d) \Rightarrow 20a + (60\cdot59 - 40\cdot39)d = 0 \Rightarrow a + 99d = 0\). Hence \(a_{100} = a + 99d = 0\).

Let the three terms be \(a-d, a, a+d\). Sum \(= 3a = 21 \Rightarrow a = 7\). Product of first and third \(= a^2 - d^2 = 45 \Rightarrow 49 - d^2 = 45 \Rightarrow d = \pm 2\). The numbers are \(5, 7, 9\), product \(= 315\).
In A.P. the middle term is the average: \(2(2a+1) = (a+1) + (4a-1) \Rightarrow 4a + 2 = 5a \Rightarrow a = 2\).

Rationalise each term: \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a_k}+\sqrt{a_{k+1}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{a_{k+1}}-\sqrt{a_k}}{a_{k+1}-a_k} = \dfrac{\sqrt{a_{k+1}}-\sqrt{a_k}}{d}\). The sum telescopes to \(\dfrac{\sqrt{a_4}-\sqrt{a_1}}{d} = \dfrac{\sqrt{a_4}-\sqrt{a_1}}{a_3 - a_2}\).

\(\log_a x, \log_b x, \log_c x\) in A.P. gives \(\dfrac{2}{\log_b x} = \dfrac{1}{\log_a x} + \dfrac{1}{\log_c x}\), i.e. \(2\log_x b = \log_x a + \log_x c\). Simplifying leads to \(c^2 = (ac)^{\log_a b}\).

\(x = 1\) is always a root since \((b-c)+(c-a)+(a-b) = 0\). Equal roots \(\Rightarrow\) both roots are 1, so product \(= \dfrac{a-b}{b-c} = 1 \Rightarrow a-b = b-c \Rightarrow 2b = a+c\). Thus \(a, b, c\) are in A.P.

Angles in A.P. \(\Rightarrow\) the middle angle is \(60^\circ\), opposite the third side. With the other two sides 9 and 10 and included angle \(60^\circ\): third side \(= \sqrt{9^2 + 10^2 - 2(9)(10)\cos 60^\circ} = \sqrt{81 + 100 - 90} = \sqrt{91}\).
A.P. with \(a = 8-6i,\ d = -1+2i\). \(T_n = (8-(n-1)) + i(-6 + 2(n-1))\) is purely imaginary when \(8-(n-1) = 0 \Rightarrow n = 9\).
Using \(\dfrac{S_m}{S_n} = \dfrac{m^2}{n^2}\) for an A.P. gives \(\dfrac{a_m}{a_n} = \dfrac{2m-1}{2n-1}\).

Let the roots be \(p-d, p, p+d\). Sum \(= 3p = -a \Rightarrow p = -\tfrac{a}{3}\), which is a root: \((-\tfrac{a}{3})^3 + a(-\tfrac{a}{3})^2 + b(-\tfrac{a}{3}) + c = 0\). Multiplying by 27: \(2a^3 - 9ab + 27c = 0 \Rightarrow 2a^3 - 9ab = -27c\).
\(S_{10} = \tfrac12(S_{20}-S_{10}) \Rightarrow 3S_{10} = S_{20} \Rightarrow 10a = 55d \Rightarrow a = 5.5d\). \(a_2 = a + d = 6.5d = 13 \Rightarrow d = 2\).
Take terms \(a-3d, a-d, a+d, a+3d\). \(a_1 + a_4 = 2a = 10 \Rightarrow a = 5\); \(a_2 a_3 = a^2 - d^2 = 24 \Rightarrow d = 1\). Terms: \(2, 4, 6, 8\); least \(= 2\).

First three months: \(3 \times 200 = 600\). From month 4 the increments form an A.P.: total \(= 3(200) + \tfrac{(n-3)}{2}[2(240) + (n-4)40] = 11040\), giving \(n^2 + 5n - 546 = 0 \Rightarrow (n+26)(n-21) = 0 \Rightarrow n = 21\).
For an A.P., \(S_1, S_2-S_1, S_3-S_2\) (sums of successive blocks of \(n\)) themselves form an A.P., giving \(S_3 = 3(S_2 - S_1)\).
\(4^x = 16^y = 64^z \Rightarrow 2x = 4y = 6z\). So \(\tfrac1x : \tfrac1y : \tfrac1z = 2 : 4 : 6\), i.e. \(\tfrac1x, \tfrac1y, \tfrac1z\) are in A.P.
A.P. with \(a = 135,\ d = 15\). \(S_n = \tfrac{n}{2}[2(135) + (n-1)15] = 5550 \Rightarrow n^2 + 17n - 740 = 0 \Rightarrow (n-20)(n+37) = 0 \Rightarrow n = 20\).
From \(a, 9, 3a-b, 3a+b\) in A.P.: equal common differences give \(a = 5,\ b = 2\), so the A.P. is \(5, 9, 13, 17, \ldots\) with \(d = 4\). \(a_{2011} = 5 + 2010(4) = 8045\).

First 10 minutes: \(10 \times 150 = 1500\), leaving \(3000\). From the 11th minute the counts form an A.P. starting 148 with \(d = -2\): \(\tfrac{m}{2}[2(148) + (m-1)(-2)] = 3000 \Rightarrow m(149-m) = 3000 \Rightarrow m = 24\) (taking the meaningful root). Total time \(= 10 + 24 = 34\) minutes.
Differences \(2, 4, 6, \ldots\) are an A.P., so \(T_n\) is quadratic: \(T_n = n^2 - n + 1\). \(n^2 - n + 1 = 9901 \Rightarrow n^2 - n - 9900 = 0 \Rightarrow (n-100)(n+99) = 0 \Rightarrow n = 100\).

Sum to \(2n\) of \(2,5,8,\ldots\) equals sum to \(n\) of \(57,59,\ldots\): \(\tfrac{2n}{2}[4 + (2n-1)3] = \tfrac{n}{2}[114 + (n-1)2]\), i.e. \(n(6n+1) = n(n+56) \Rightarrow 5n = 55 \Rightarrow n = 11\).
Each term \(\sin d \sec a_k \sec a_{k+1} = \dfrac{\sin(a_{k+1}-a_k)}{\cos a_k \cos a_{k+1}} = \tan a_{k+1} - \tan a_k\). The sum telescopes to \(\tan a_n - \tan a_1\).
With the wrong \(d = -3\): \(\tfrac{10}{2}[2a + 9(-3)] = -30 \Rightarrow 2a - 27 = -6 \Rightarrow a = \tfrac{21}{2}\). Actual sum with \(d = 3\): \(\tfrac{10}{2}[21 + 9(3)] = 5(48) = 240\).
\(a_p = q,\ a_q = p \Rightarrow (q-p) = (p-q)d \Rightarrow d = -1\), and \(a = p+q-1\). Then \(a_{10} = a + 9d = (p+q-1) - 9 = p+q-10\).

Add 1 to each term: \(\dfrac{a+b+c}{b+c}, \dfrac{a+b+c}{c+a}, \dfrac{a+b+c}{a+b}\) in A.P. \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{b+c}, \dfrac{1}{c+a}, \dfrac{1}{a+b}\) in A.P. Clearing leads to \(2b^2 = a^2 + c^2\), i.e. \(a^2, b^2, c^2\) are in A.P.
Each term equals the sum of the next two: \(ar^{n} = ar^{n+1} + ar^{n+2} \Rightarrow 1 = r + r^2 \Rightarrow r^2 + r - 1 = 0\). Positive terms \(\Rightarrow r = \dfrac{\sqrt5 - 1}{2}\).

\(\cos^2\theta = (1-\sin\theta)\tan\theta \Rightarrow \cos^3\theta = \sin^2\theta(1-\sin\theta)\cdots\) simplifying gives \(\cos\theta = \cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}\), so \(\theta = 2n\pi \pm \tfrac{\pi}{3}\).
\(x = \tfrac{a+b}{2},\ y = \tfrac{b+c}{2}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{2x} + \dfrac{1}{2y} = \dfrac{1}{a+b} + \dfrac{1}{b+c}\). With \(b^2 = ac\) this simplifies to \(\dfrac{1}{b}\).
The 11 terms are symmetric about the 6th term, so their product \(= (\text{6th term})^{11} = 2^{11} = 2048\).
The inequality is \((ap-b)^2 + (bp-c)^2 + (cp-d)^2 \le 0\), forcing each square to vanish: \(\dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{c}{b} = \dfrac{d}{c} = p\). Hence \(a, b, c, d\) are in G.P.
Roots in G.P. \(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}, \alpha, \alpha r\) have product \(\alpha^3 = 8 \Rightarrow \alpha = 2\). Since 2 is a root: \(8 - 4k + 28 - 8 = 0 \Rightarrow k = 7\).

Areas form a G.P. \(25, \tfrac{25}{2}, \tfrac{25}{4}, \ldots\) (\(r = \tfrac12\), each new square has half the area). Sum of 10 terms \(= \dfrac{25(1 - (1/2)^{10})}{1 - 1/2} = 50\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2^{10}}\right)\).
Let the G.P. be \(a, ar, ar^2\). Doubling the middle gives an A.P.: \(2(2ar) = a + ar^2 \Rightarrow r^2 - 4r + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow r = 2 \pm \sqrt3\). Increasing \(\Rightarrow r = 2 + \sqrt3\).

Putting \(x = 1\): \(\log_c a - 2\log_c b + \log_c c = \log_c\tfrac{ac}{b^2}\); since \(b^2 = ac\) this is \(\log_c 1 = 0\), so \(x = 1\) is a root. The product of the roots \(= \dfrac{\log_c c}{\log_c a} = \log_a c\), so the other root is \(\log_a c\). Roots: \(1\) and \(\log_a c\).
Take the five terms as \(a-2d, a-d, a, a+d, a+2d\). The 1st, 3rd, 4th in G.P.: \(a^2 = (a-2d)(a+d) \Rightarrow 2d^2 = -ad \Rightarrow a = -2d\). Then the 5th term \(= a + 2d = 0\).
With G.P. terms \(ar^{p-1} = 64,\ ar^{q-1} = 27,\ ar^{r-1} = 36\): dividing gives \(r^{p-q} = (\tfrac43)^3\) and \(r^{q-r} = \tfrac34\). Eliminating leads to \(p + 2q = 3r\).

\(\dfrac{a+2}{2} - \sqrt{2a} = 1 \Rightarrow a + 2 - 2\sqrt{2a} = 2 \Rightarrow a = 2\sqrt{2a} \Rightarrow a^2 = 8a \Rightarrow a(a-8) = 0\). As \(a > 0\), \(a = 8\). [Source answer key prints 'c' (9), which is inconsistent with this derivation.]
\(\sin\theta, \cos\theta, \tan\theta\) in G.P. \(\Rightarrow \cos^2\theta = \sin\theta\tan\theta\). Simplifying gives \(\cot^6\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\).
A.M. 9 \(\Rightarrow x+y = 18\); G.M. 4 \(\Rightarrow xy = 16\). So \(x, y\) are roots of \(t^2 - 18t + 16 = 0\).

\(\sqrt3 = \tan(A+B) = \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B}\). Writing \(s = \tan A + \tan B\) and using A.M.\(\ge\)G.M. on \(\tan A, \tan B\) gives \(s^2 + 4\sqrt3\,s - 4 \ge 0\), whose positive bound is \(s = 4 - 2\sqrt3\).

\(11^3 + \ldots + 20^3 = \left(\tfrac{20\cdot21}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\tfrac{10\cdot11}{2}\right)^2 = 210^2 - 55^2 = 44100 - 3025 = 41075 = 5 \times 8215\). This is an odd integer divisible by 5. [Source answer key prints 'a' (even), which contradicts the value 41075.]
\(\tfrac{n(n+1)}{2} = \tfrac15 \cdot \tfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} \Rightarrow \tfrac12 = \tfrac{2n+1}{30} \Rightarrow 2n+1 = 15 \Rightarrow n = 7\). Hence (C).
Two-digit numbers \(\equiv 5 \pmod 7\): \(12, 19, \ldots, 96\), an A.P. with 13 terms. Sum \(= \tfrac{13}{2}(12 + 96) = 13 \times 54 = 702\).

Infinite G.P.: \(\dfrac{1}{1-\sin\theta} = 2\sqrt3 + 4 \Rightarrow 1 - \sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{4+2\sqrt3} = 1 - \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} \Rightarrow \sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\).

\(S_k = \dfrac{k}{1 - \frac{k}{k+1}} = k(k+1)\), so \(\dfrac{1}{S_k} = \dfrac1k - \dfrac{1}{k+1}\). Then \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{(-1)^k}{S_k} = \sum (-1)^k\left(\dfrac1k - \dfrac{1}{k+1}\right) = -\log_e 2 - (\log_e 2 - 1) = 1 - 2\log_e 2 = 1 - \log_e 4\).
\(\dfrac{a}{1-r} = \dfrac43\) with \(a = \dfrac34\): \(\dfrac{3/4}{1-r} = \dfrac43 \Rightarrow 1 - r = \dfrac{9}{16} \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{7}{16}\).

Inner sum \(\tfrac13 + \tfrac{1}{3^2} + \ldots = \dfrac{1/3}{1 - 1/3} = \dfrac12\). Since \(0.16 = (2.5)^{-2}\), \((0.16)^{\log_{2.5}(1/2)} = (2.5)^{-2\log_{2.5}(1/2)} = (1/2)^{-2} = 4\). The outer \(\tfrac12\) power gives \(\sqrt4 = 2\). As \(2\) is none of \(1, -1, 0\), the answer is 'None of these'. [Source answer key prints 'a' (1), which is inconsistent with this value.]
\(H = 4 \Rightarrow \dfrac{2ab}{a+b} = 4\); \(2A + G^2 = (a+b) + ab = 27\). Solving \(ab = 2(a+b)\) and \((a+b) + ab = 27\) gives \(a+b = 9,\ ab = 18\), so the numbers are \(3\) and \(6\).
\(x = \dfrac{1}{1-a},\ y = \dfrac{1}{1-b},\ z = \dfrac{1}{1-c}\). Since \(a, b, c\) in A.P., \(1-a, 1-b, 1-c\) are in A.P., so their reciprocals \(x, y, z\) are in H.P.
If \(a, b, c\) are in H.P. then \(\dfrac{a}{b+c}, \dfrac{b}{c+a}, \dfrac{c}{a+b}\) are also in H.P. (dividing the H.P. relation by \(a+b+c\)).
\(H = \dfrac{2PQ}{P+Q}\). \(\dfrac{H}{P} + \dfrac{H}{Q} = H\left(\dfrac1P + \dfrac1Q\right) = \dfrac{2PQ}{P+Q}\cdot\dfrac{P+Q}{PQ} = 2\).

A.P.: \(d = \dfrac{3-2}{9} = \dfrac19\), so \(a_4 = 2 + 3(\tfrac19) = \tfrac73\). H.P.: \(\tfrac{1}{h_1} = \tfrac12, \tfrac{1}{h_{10}} = \tfrac13\), giving \(\tfrac{1}{h_7} = \tfrac{7}{18}\), so \(h_7 = \tfrac{18}{7}\). Hence \(a_4 h_7 = \tfrac73 \cdot \tfrac{18}{7} = 6\).
G.M. 10 \(\Rightarrow ab = 100\); H.M. 8 \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{2ab}{a+b} = 8 \Rightarrow a+b = 25\). Roots of \(t^2 - 25t + 100 = 0\): \(5\) and \(20\).

\(\log(x+z) + \log(x-2y+z) = 2\log(x-z) \Rightarrow (x+z)(x-2y+z) = (x-z)^2\). Expanding gives \(2xz = xy + yz \Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{y} = \dfrac1x + \dfrac1z\), so \(x, y, z\) are in H.P. [Source answer key prints 'b' (A.P.), which contradicts this derivation.]

Reciprocals \(\tfrac52, \tfrac{13}{12}\) are in A.P. with \(d = \tfrac{13}{12} - \tfrac52 = -\tfrac{17}{12}\); the 3rd reciprocal onward is negative, so the corresponding H.P. terms are negative. The largest positive H.P. term is the 2nd term, \(\tfrac{12}{13}\).
G.M. \(\sqrt{ab} = 24 \Rightarrow ab = 576\); H.M. \(\dfrac{2ab}{a+b} = \tfrac{72}{5} \Rightarrow a+b = 80\). Roots of \(t^2 - 80t + 576 = 0\): \(8\) and \(72\); greater is 72.

\(\dfrac{2}{(1-x)(2-x)} = \dfrac{2}{1-x} - \dfrac{2}{2-x} = 2\sum x^n - \sum (x/2)^n\). Coefficient of \(x^3 = 2 - (1/2)^3 = 2 - \tfrac18 = \tfrac{15}{8}\). [Source answer key prints 'd' (15/16), inconsistent with this expansion.]

\(\tan\tfrac{C}{2} = \cot\tfrac{A+B}{2} = \dfrac{1 - \tan\frac{A}{2}\tan\frac{B}{2}}{\tan\frac{A}{2} + \tan\frac{B}{2}} = \dfrac25\). Then \(\sin A = \tfrac{60}{61}, \sin B = \tfrac{1480}{1769}, \sin C = \tfrac{20}{29}\); these (and hence the sides) are in A.P. (each successive difference is equal).

Each term \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{k+1}-\sqrt{k}} = \sqrt{k+1}+\sqrt{k}\). With the alternating signs the sum is \((\sqrt{10}+\sqrt9) - (\sqrt{11}+\sqrt{10}) + (\sqrt{12}+\sqrt{11}) - \ldots - (\sqrt{121}+\sqrt{120})\); all interior \(\sqrt{k}\) cancel, leaving \(\sqrt9 - \sqrt{121} = 3 - 11 = -8\).
Each term \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3k-1}+\sqrt{3k+2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3k+2}-\sqrt{3k-1}}{3}\). The sum telescopes to \(\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\sqrt{3n+2} - \sqrt2\right)\).

Let \(O = \sum \tfrac{1}{(2k-1)^2}\) (odd) and \(E = \sum \tfrac{1}{(2k)^2} = \tfrac14\cdot\tfrac{\pi^2}{6} = \tfrac{\pi^2}{24}\) (even). Then \(O = \tfrac{\pi^2}{6} - \tfrac{\pi^2}{24} = \tfrac{\pi^2}{8}\).
